query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A high entropy alloy (HEA) coating can be used to adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix to enhance its wear resistance.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable oxide film
generation.mechanism: Protection of the underlying material by tribo-oxidation and the formation of a stable oxide film
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced wear resistance of the Cu matrix
generation.baseline: Wear resistance of the Cu matrix without HEA coating
generation.uncertainty: The optimal composition and processing conditions of the HEA coating for maximum wear resistance

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear resistance of the Cu matrix with HEA coating is not significantly higher than that without HEA coating, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 SPS sample. Intervention: Reciprocating wear test at 650 °C. Processing: Force 26 N, Frequency 40 Hz, Time 900 s, Amplitude 0.5 mm, Counter Body Al2O3. Test conditions: 650 °C, atmospherical conditions. Structure change: Surface incompletely covered with oxides; oxides are less rough and exhibit grooves in wear direction; formation of an interrupted oxide layer. Property change: Wear depth slightly decreased compared to 500 °C (increased wear resistance); high standard deviation of COF. Mechanism: Increasing stability caused by a rise in thickness and hence a protection of the underlying metallic material. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The surface of the sample tested at a temperature of 650 °C is also incompletely covered with oxides."

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 SPS sample. Intervention: Reciprocating wear test at 800 °C. Processing: Force 26 N, Frequency 40 Hz, Time 900 s, Amplitude 0.5 mm, Counter Body Al2O3. Test conditions: 800 °C, atmospherical conditions. Structure change: Almost fully oxide-covered surface, relatively smooth with some grooves; spinel phase detected by XRD. Property change: Distinct reduction in wear depth (high wear resistance) compared to lower temperatures. Mechanism: Protection of the underlying material by tribo-oxidation and the formation of a stable oxide film. Evidence: measured. Quote: "For the wear investigations at 800 °C, a distinct reduction in wear depth occurs."

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 SPS sample. Intervention: Reciprocating wear test at 900 °C. Processing: Force 26 N, Frequency 40 Hz, Time 900 s, Amplitude 0.5 mm, Counter Body Al2O3. Test conditions: 900 °C, atmospherical conditions. Structure change: Abrasive wear of the oxides observed on the smooth, fully oxide-covered surface. Property change: Highest wear resistance; COF of 0.85. Mechanism: Abrasive wear of the oxides. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The decrease in wear depth proves the protection of the underlying material by tribo-oxidation and the formaton of a stable oxide film."
